reviewMethod: Actual established original source sheet plus final front/profile CPU pixels and predecessor comparisons inspected one image per call. Read-only hash checks; no authoring, publication, candidate mutation or engine/GPU retest.
limitations: Only two focused final views per candidate. No full-body/weapon detail set is certified.
Source illustration and candidate lighting/cameras are not calibrated; no exact dimensions/anatomical ratios inferred.
Pixel review does not prove topology, UVs, optics parity, collision, animation quality, performance or engine compatibility.
concreteImprovement: Crystal faces are visibly more varied and faceted than the flatter V12 strip, with distinct angular highlights/planes; stone relief/overlaps are more articulated. This is a real local visual improvement, not an exact construction match.

findings.finding: The interior still reads as one long connected central channel despite improved facets. Source053 has a more irregular substantial interior with changing exposure/occlusion and interlocking crystal clusters; that composition remains unmatched.

Large similarly scaled primary stone banks remain tile-like. Added small facets/terraces increase detail, but the profile still reveals long near-parallel substrate edges around the center instead of source-defined interleaved fracture hierarchy.

The guard remains a bulky cylindrical/cuff structure with regular flange rhythm; source fitted irregular bronze-and-stone enclosure and studs are absent. Pommel remains one long purple prism in sparse shell pieces rather than a compact fractured cluster.

Broad regular leather wraps and thin repeating seam rhythm remain; bronze/stone material divisions and localized source wear are simplified. Warmer leather color is retained but does not fix wrap construction.

recommendedPriority: Keep the stronger facet/depth direction, then address the primary bank/channel composition and guard/pommel silhouettes. Do not use microfracture detail as a substitute for the larger construction differences. No new authoring was performed.
